info.description: Pirate ships race around a ring of islands digging up buried treasure. Every island you stop at hands you treasure, forces treasure on you or lets you rob the captain moored there, while a wandering storm blows ships and cargo across the sea and a hold of more than seven treasure capsizes. The first captain to land ten treasure in their own harbour wins.
info.ruleText:
Several pirate ships cruise a ring of 28 lonely islands looking for buried treasure. Dig it up, load it on board and be the first to bring ten pieces safely into your own harbour - while a wandering storm, greedy rivals and your own overloaded hold do their best to stop you.

On your turn you roll one die. A number sails your ship that many islands onward, following the arrows; an island has room for two ships, a third one sails on to the next free island. Islands with an open chest let you take as much of the treasure as you like, up to the number on the chest - half of them hold at most one, the other half up to three; a closed red chest blinds you with greed and forces two on board; on an island without a chest the arriving captain may take up to two treasure from the ship moored there, or push up to two onto it. A hold takes seven treasure at most - one too many and the ship capsizes and the whole cargo sinks.

Each colour has a harbour beside its own entrance island. Only its owner may turn in, and the rest of the move is lost when they do; the treasure is unloaded there and the ship sets out again on the next turn.

The storm face of the die lets you sail one single island and then drift the storm against the sailing direction - up to five islands with two players, four with three, three with four. If the storm comes to rest on an island with ships, the wind wheel decides their fate: blown one island on, one treasure to every other captain, swept safely home, or two treasure washed into the sea.
info.helpText:
Goal

Be the first captain to land 10 treasure in your own harbour. The number on your harbour plate - and the anchor counter next to your seat - is what you have landed so far.

The treasure

Treasure is real gold coins. They wait in the sunken chest in the middle of the sea, they stack up on the deck of your ship while you sail - the taller the stack, the closer you are to capsizing - and they pile up in your harbour once you land them. Ten coins in your harbour win the game. The dice button carries them for you, but you can also pick any coin up and drag it wherever you want.

Setup

Everybody clicks a seat - the coloured sailboat at the left of each seat row shows which ship that seat commands - then somebody presses the round brown new voyage button (the circling arrows) on the right. All ships return to their harbours, the storm is placed on a random island and a random captain starts. Until then a hint plate in the middle of the sea points at that button.

Your turn

Press the big gold dice button on the right (or click the die itself); its border is drawn in the colour of the captain whose turn it is. Everything that follows is worked out for you; you only answer the questions. The ? button at the top of the panel repeats all of this at the table.
  • A number - your ship sails that many islands clockwise, following the dark arrows. If your own harbour entrance is on the way you are asked whether you want to sail in, unload and start a new voyage; the rest of the move is then lost.
  • The storm symbol - you may first sail on one single island, then you drift the storm against the sailing direction (the white wind arrows): up to 5 islands with 2 players, 4 with 3 players, 3 with 4 players (0 = leave it where it is).

The 28 spaces

  • Open chest, green 1 - load as much treasure as you like, 0 or 1.
  • Open chest, green 3 - load as much treasure as you like, 0 to 3. Half of the open chests are the small ones, half the big ones. The dialog suggests the largest amount your hold can take.
  • Closed chest, red 2 - greed wins: you must load 2 treasure.
  • Island without a chest - if a rival ship is moored here you may steal up to 2 treasure from it, or push up to 2 of yours onto it to make it capsize. Choose nothing to leave both ships alone.
  • Harbour entrance - the anchor island in each corner. The harbour itself lies beside it and only its owner may sail in.
  • An island has room for two ships; a third one sails on to the next island with a free berth.
  • A ship carries at most 7 treasure. Load more and it capsizes: the whole cargo sinks back into the chest in the sea and the ship sails on with an empty hold.

When the storm comes to rest on ships

The wind wheel in the middle of the sea is spun and shows what happens to every ship on that island:
  • Wind - the ships are blown one island onward and work that island as usual.
  • Three figures - each hit ship hands one treasure to every other captain, who has to take it aboard - a full hold capsizes. A captain lying in their harbour puts it straight into the harbour.
  • Anchor - lucky! The hit ships reach their own harbour and unload at once.
  • Splash - two coins per hit ship wash back into the sea.

Playing by hand

Nothing is ever blocked. Every coin can simply be dragged - out of the sunken chest, onto a ship, from one ship to another, into a harbour - and the two counters follow along on their own. Ships and the storm can be dragged from island to island in the same way, and the two counters next to your seat can still be clicked to set the cargo on board (⛵) and the treasure in your harbour (⚓) as a number, which moves the matching coins for you - useful for house rules, for taking a move back or for setting up a position. A piece that is not on a space glows red, so a ship left in open water is easy to spot and to drop onto an island. The dice button is only the comfortable way to play.

Winning

The winner is announced on a laurel banner in the middle of the sea; click the banner to push it aside. The hint plate underneath points back at the new-voyage button.

Shorter game

Agree on fewer than 10 treasure before you start and simply stop when somebody reaches that number - the anchor counter next to each seat shows the score.

How to play
Goal: be the first captain to land 10 treasure in your own harbour.
1. Press the round brown button to start a new voyage - every ship goes back to its own harbour and the storm is placed at random.
2. On your turn press the gold button (or the die). Sail your ship that many islands along the arrows.
3. Green island with a green number: take up to that many treasure. Island with a red 2: you must take 2.
4. Plain island: if a rival ship is there you may take up to 2 treasure from it - or push up to 2 of yours onto it to sink it.
More than 7 treasure on board and your ship capsizes: the whole cargo sinks back into the hoard.
6. Sail past your own harbour to turn in and unload. The rest of the move is lost, the treasure is safe.
7. Tornado on the die: you may sail one island, then you drift the storm backwards along the route. Every ship the storm reaches spins the wind wheel in the middle of the sea.
The wind wheel

Gust (top left): the ship is blown one island onwards. Three friends (top right): the ship gives one treasure to every other ship. Anchor (bottom right): the ship is carried home and unloads. Splash (bottom left): the ship loses 2 treasure.
The treasure

Treasure is real gold coins. They wait in the sunken hoard in the middle of the sea, stack up on the deck of your ship while you sail - the taller the stack, the closer you are to capsizing - and pile up in your harbour once you land them. Ten coins in your harbour win the game.
Playing by hand

Nothing is ever blocked. Drag the gold coins yourself - out of the sunken hoard, onto a ship, from one ship to another, into a harbour - and the counters follow. Ships and the storm can be dragged from island to island as well, and the two round counters beside your name still let you correct cargo and landed treasure with a number. A ship that is not on a space glows red.
